title: Overlap Extension PCR Protocol
author: Anna Behle
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.psndnde

steps.title: Design Primers In Silico
steps.instruction: Plan the experiment using cloning software (e.g., SnapGene) to ensure primers anneal only once to the template and that separate parts can anneal to each other after PCR.

substeps.instruction: Ensure annealing parts of primers bind to template only once with a Tm of 55-65 °C.
Ensure total overlap between two fragments has a Tm of at least 55 °C to avoid unspecific binding.
Optionally add overhangs to the desired vector backbone to the primers flanking the fused part (e.g., P1 and P6) to facilitate downstream cloning.

steps.title: Amplify and Purify Individual Fragments
steps.instruction: Prepare separate PCR reactions for each part to be assembled using Q5 High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase (NEB #M0491S).

substeps.instruction: Set annealing temperatures based on the part of the primer annealing to the template, disregarding the overhang.
Gel-purify fragments of the correct size using a Gel and PCR Clean-up kit (Macherey-Nagel #740609.250).

steps.title: Perform Initial Overlap Extension PCR
steps.instruction: Run a 15-cycle PCR without primers to assemble the fragments using the annealing temperature of the homologous regions.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the PCR mixture using a molar ratio of ~1:1 for fragments, recommending 50 ng of the larger PCR fragment.
Use a large volume for templates (1/2 to 3/4 of total reaction) to account for low concentration of gel-extracted fragments.

Assemble the reaction (example for Q5-Polymerase): 5 µL 5x buffer, 5 µL 5x high GC buffer, 0.5 µL dNTPs, 4 µL template, 5 µL fragment 1, 5 µL fragment 2, 5 µL fragment 3, 0.5 µL Q5 Polymerase, and H2O up to 25 µL.
Remove PCR from cycler and immediately proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Amplify Assembled Product
steps.instruction: Add the two primers flanking the outer parts and rerun the PCR for 30 cycles.

substeps.instruction: Use an annealing temperature matching the flanking primers.
Gel-extract the final overlap extension product to remove non-specific side products, smears, or original fragments.
